# QZX support

QZX is free, open source, and built to make cross-platform work more
predictable for people, automation, and AI agents. The following routes help a
question reach the right place.

## Usage questions and ideas

Use [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/alesanGreat/QZX-Quick-Zap-Exchange/discussions)
for setup help, command usage, integration questions, and early ideas. Before
posting, check the [command catalog](https://qzx.yumbale.com/en/commands) and
ask the installed runtime what it supports:

```console
qzx version --json
qzx listCommands --json
```

## Reproducible bugs and platform evidence

Use the [issue chooser](https://github.com/alesanGreat/QZX-Quick-Zap-Exchange/issues/new/choose)
for a reproducible bug, feature proposal, or platform evidence report. Use the
specialized Golden Core form for a canonical cohort capture and the general
platform-evidence form for any other command or bounded observation. Include
the exact QZX revision and version, environment, command, exit status,
limitations, and manually reviewed sanitized output when relevant.

## Private security reports

Potential vulnerabilities belong in the repository's
[security policy](https://github.com/alesanGreat/QZX-Quick-Zap-Exchange/security/policy),
which lists the private vulnerability report and email fallback. Do not use a
public issue or discussion.

## Sponsorship

Questions about funding an open, bounded project outcome can be sent to
`qzx@yumbale.com`. The project's independence and recognition policy is
described in [SPONSORSHIP.md](../SPONSORSHIP.md).
